task.task_name: Triage a personal auto collision claim
task.task_description: You handle new auto insurance claims. A policyholder reports a two-car collision at an intersection and sends in their account of what happened, vehicle details, damage photos, the other driver's contact and insurance information, and a police report number. Some details might be missing or conflicting, and there may not be a repair estimate yet. Your task is to check the claim against the policy and available records, see whether there's enough information to move it forward, flag missing documents or possible coverage issues, and send it to the right claims team. Straightforward claims can go through the usual process. Claims involving injuries, conflicting accounts, signs of possible fraud, or complicated coverage questions need specialist attention. You're getting the claim ready for an adjuster, who will make the final coverage and liability decisions.

operational_subtasks.description: Review the policyholder's account, vehicle and driver details, damage photos, other driver's information, and police report number; identify the reported loss facts and any apparent gaps or inconsistencies.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one submitted packet per claim and a routine first review of the supplied materials; allow about 8 minutes to read and organize the facts without separately re-reviewing them later.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Compare claim facts with available records
operational_subtasks.description: Check relevant available claim and incident records, including any accessible police report information, against the reported loss details; note material discrepancies without making a liability determination.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one records check per claim and that relevant records can be consulted through ordinary internal systems; allow about 6 minutes for targeted comparison, not for obtaining unavailable records or resolving liability.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Check policy applicability and potential coverage issues
operational_subtasks.description: Review the policy and available policy records for applicability to the reported loss, including relevant dates, insured parties and vehicles, and terms that may raise a coverage question; flag potential issues for the adjuster.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one initial policy check per claim using the reported facts and accessible policy records; allow about 7 minutes for an initial applicability review and issue identification, not a final coverage decision.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Assess information sufficiency and missing items
operational_subtasks.description: Determine whether the available information is sufficient to move the claim into the next claims process; identify missing documents or details, considering whether an absent repair estimate is needed at this stage.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one sufficiency assessment per claim, using findings already gathered; allow about 4 minutes for the incremental check against intake needs without repeating the document review.

operational_subtasks.description: Evaluate the available information for reported injuries, conflicting accounts, possible fraud indicators, or complicated coverage questions that warrant specialist attention.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume every claim receives this initial screen; allow about 4 minutes for the incremental evaluation of the stated escalation indicators using findings already available, without conducting a separate fraud or liability investigation.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Prepare and route the claim triage handoff
operational_subtasks.description: Send the claim to the appropriate standard or specialist claims team with a concise summary of the reported facts, sufficiency, missing items, relevant discrepancies, and potential coverage or escalation issues.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assume one handoff per claim; allow about 3 minutes to select the destination and convey the findings using the completed review, without repeating the underlying analysis.

parent_output_contract.completion_boundary: The available claim and policy information has been reviewed, sufficiency and potential issues have been identified, and the claim with those findings has been sent to the appropriate claims team.
